The goal is to minimize the total transportation cost while ensuring that all cities receive the resources they need, without exceeding the capacity of the transportation links or the storage capacity of the cities.

The cost of transporting resources from City 0 to City 1 is 1 unit, to City 2 is 1 unit, to City 3 is 1 unit, to City 4 is 1 unit, to City 5 is 3 units, to City 6 is 3 units, and to City 7 is 3 units. From City 1 to City 0 is 1 unit, to City 2 is 2 units, to City 3 is 2 units, to City 4 is 2 units, to City 5 is 3 units, to City 6 is 2 units, and to City 7 is 1 unit. From City 2 to City 0 is 2 units, to City 1 is 3 units, to City 3 is 3 units, to City 4 is 2 units, to City 5 is 2 units, to City 6 is 3 units, and to City 7 is 3 units. From City 6 to City 0 is 2 units, to City 1 is 3 units, to City 2 is 3 units, to City 3 is 2 units, to City 4 is 3 units, to City 5 is 1 unit, and to City 7 is 1 unit. From City 7 to City 0 is 2 units, to City 1 is 1 unit, to City 2 is 2 units, to City 3 is 2 units, to City 4 is 1 unit, to City 5 is 1 unit, and to City 6 is 1 unit.

The maximum capacity for transporting resources from City 0 to City 1 is 7 units, to City 2 is 9 units, to City 3 is 7 units, to City 4 is 8 units, to City 5 is 9 units, to City 6 is 7 units, and to City 7 is 7 units. From City 1 to City 0 is 8 units, to City 2 is 8 units, to City 3 is 8 units, to City 4 is 7 units, to City 5 is 9 units, to City 6 is 8 units, and to City 7 is 9 units. def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["num_cities"]
    cities = list(range(n))
    links = list(d["cost"].keys())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets -------------------------------------------------------------
    model.CITIES = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.LINKS = pyo.Set(initialize=links, dimen=2, ordered=True)

    # --- Variables --------------------------------------------------------
    # Amount transported on each directed link; bounds = link capacity.
    def flow_bounds(m, i, j):
        return (0, d["link_cap"][(i, j)])

    model.flow = pyo.Var(
        model.LINKS,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=flow_bounds,
    )

    # Storage held at each city; bounded by storage capacity.
    def store_bounds(m, i):
        return (0, d["storage_cap"][i])

    model.storage = pyo.Var(
        model.CITIES,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=store_bounds,
    )

    # --- Objective: minimize total transportation cost --------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost"][(i, j)] * m.flow[i, j] for (i, j) in links)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # --- Constraints ------------------------------------------------------

    # Link capacity: flow on each link must not exceed its capacity.
    def link_cap_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.flow[i, j] <= d["link_cap"][(i, j)]

    model.link_capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.LINKS, rule=link_cap_rule)

    # Storage capacity: stored amount at each city must not exceed its cap.
    def store_cap_rule(m, i):
        return m.storage[i] <= d["storage_cap"][i]

    model.storage_capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.CITIES, rule=store_cap_rule)

    # Net balance: own net supply + inflow - outflow = storage held.
    # (Net supply is negative for demand cities, satisfying their demand.)
    def balance_rule(m, i):
        inflow = sum(m.flow[j, i] for (j, k) in links if k == i)
        outflow = sum(m.flow[i, j] for (k, j) in links if k == i)
        return d["net_supply"][i] + inflow - outflow == m.storage[i]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.CITIES, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

    d = data or DATA
    cities = sorted(d["net_balance"].keys())
    links = [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.LINKS = pyo.Set(initialize=links, dimen=2)

    # Decision variable: units transported from i to j
    model.flow = pyo.Var(
        model.LINKS,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=lambda m, i, j: (0, d["capacity"][i][j]),
    )

    # Objective: minimise total transportation cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost"][i][j] * m.flow[i, j] for (i, j) in m.LINKS)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Flow conservation / net balance at each city
    # inflow - outflow == net_balance  (positive balance = net demand)
    def balance_rule(m, k):
        inflow = sum(m.flow[j, k] for (j, kk) in m.LINKS if kk == k)
        outflow = sum(m.flow[k, j] for (kk, j) in m.LINKS if kk == k)
        return inflow - outflow == d["net_balance"][k]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.CITIES, rule=balance_rule)

        return m.flow[i, j] <= d["capacity"][i][j]

    def storage_rule(m, k):

    model.storage_capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.CITIES, rule=storage_rule)

    return model

        inflow = sum(m.x[i, k] for (i, j) in arcs if j == k)

        return inflow <= stor[k]

    model.storage_limit = pyo.Constraint(model.Cities, rule=storage_rule)

    return model

    links = list(d["cost"].keys())  # all ordered pairs i != j

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.N = pyo.RangeSet(0, n - 1)
    # Arc set: only the directed links that have a cost/capacity given
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=links, dimen=2)

    # Decision: amount shipped along each directed link
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.A, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Link capacity upper bounds
    def cap_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[i, j] <= d["cap"][(i, j)]
    model.link_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.A, rule=cap_rule)

    # Flow balance: net outflow - net inflow = net supply (+) / demand (-)
    def balance_rule(m, i):
        outflow = sum(m.x[i, j] for (a, j) in links if a == i)
        inflow = sum(m.x[j, i] for (j, b) in links if b == i)
        return outflow - inflow == d["net"][i]
    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.N, rule=balance_rule)

    # Storage capacity: total throughput (in + out) at a city <= its storage limit
    def stor_rule(m, i):
        outflow = sum(m.x[i, j] for (a, j) in links if a == i)
        inflow = sum(m.x[j, i] for (j, b) in links if b == i)
        return outflow + inflow <= d["stor"][i]
    model.storage = pyo.Constraint(model.N, rule=stor_rule)

    # Objective: minimize total transportation cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost"][(i, j)] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in links)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model
